connection.title: Use an API key for features inside {brand}
connection.description: Only needed for the features that run inside {brand}. Your key is checked with the provider before it is saved, stored encrypted and never shown again.
connection.subscriptionNote: Have a Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Gemini subscription? Use "Connect your AI app" above: it needs no key. An API key here is only for the features that run inside {brand}: reading bills and receipts, account suggestions and the monthly summary.
connection.openRouterHint: Have an OpenRouter account? Connect it without copying a key.

connection.encryptionMissing: The server has no encryption key (INTEGRATIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY), so an API key cannot be stored yet.
connection.lastErrorAt: {date}. Until a test passes, documents may be read without AI.

consent.title: Permission to send data
consent.body: When an AI feature is on, {brand} sends the data that feature needs to {provider} under your account: uploaded bills and receipts (files or their text), your chart of accounts names for account suggestions, and monthly profit and loss totals for summaries. Nothing is sent before you agree, and AI never posts anything: you review every draft.

aiApp.title: Connect your AI app
aiApp.description: Use your own Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or Gemini subscription with {brand}. No key is needed. Your AI app can read your books and prepare drafts; a person in {brand} reviews and posts them.
aiApp.addressHint: Paste this address in your AI app, then sign in to {brand} and allow the connection.
aiApp.loadFailed: Could not load the connected AI apps.
aiApp.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
aiApp.notConfigured: Connecting an AI app is not turned on for this {brand} server yet. Ask whoever runs {brand} for your business to turn it on.
aiApp.safety: Your AI app never posts, sends, pays or deletes anything. It can only read, and prepare drafts if you allow it.

steps.claude1: In claude.ai or the Claude Desktop app, open Settings → Connectors and choose Add custom connector.
steps.claude2: Paste the {brand} address above, then choose Connect.
steps.claude3: Sign in to {brand} and allow the connection. Claude Desktop uses the same connectors as claude.ai.
steps.claudeCode1: In a terminal, run the first command below.
steps.claudeCode2: In Claude Code, type /mcp, choose {brandSlug}, then sign in to {brand} and allow the connection.
steps.chatgpt1: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode (paid ChatGPT plans; the menu names can move).
steps.chatgpt2: Choose Create, paste the {brand} address above and choose OAuth for sign-in.
steps.chatgpt3: Sign in to {brand} and allow the connection.
steps.codex1: In a terminal, run the first command below to add {brand}.
steps.codex2: Run the second command, then sign in to {brand} in the browser and allow the connection.
steps.gemini1: With Gemini CLI, run the first command below in a terminal.
steps.gemini2: In Gemini CLI, run /mcp auth {brandSlug}, then sign in to {brand} and allow the connection.
steps.gemini3: If your Gemini app shows Settings → Connected apps → Add a custom app, you can paste the {brand} address there instead.

flowline.title: Connect to FlowLine
flowline.description: Let FlowLine automations react to {brand} events and act in {brand} with a scoped key.
flowline.name: Name
flowline.encryptionMissing: Webhook secrets cannot be stored until the server administrator sets INTEGRATIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the API.

step1.title: 1. FlowLine → {brand} (API key)
step1.description: Create a key and paste it, with the API address, into FlowLine's {brand} connection.
step1.newKeyWarning: Copy it now: it will not be shown again. Anyone with this key can act with its scopes.
step1.revokeDescription: FlowLine flows using it will stop working immediately. This cannot be undone.
step1.howToUse: FlowLine sends it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>". Keys act with your role's permissions.

step2.title: 2. {brand} → FlowLine (events)
step2.description: In FlowLine, add a {brand} trigger to a flow, then paste its webhook URL and signing secret here.
step2.backlogTitle: Send reminders for old overdue invoices?
step2.backlogDescription: New webhooks only hear about invoices that become overdue after they were added. This sends every invoice that is overdue now on the next hourly check, so FlowLine reminder flows may contact all of these customers at once.
step2.backlogQueued: Overdue invoices will be sent on the next hourly check
step2.deleteDescription: {brand} stops sending events to it. Queued deliveries will fail.

log.title: Delivery log
log.description: Every event sent to FlowLine, with retries. Failed deliveries can be sent again; FlowLine ignores duplicates.

errors.WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT_INACTIVE: Enable the webhook before sending the overdue backlog.
